_about: Aristophanes in English, translator per title. Complete: The Eleven Comedies, 'now for the first time literally and completely translated' (anonymous, The Athenian Society, 1912), 2 vols. Single plays: W. J. Hickie's prose Clouds (Bohn), B. B. Rogers's verse Frogs, Jack Lindsay's Lysistrata (1926; Gutenberg treats it as US public domain; Lindsay d. 1990, so not PD in life+70 countries). PG 3012, 2571 and 3013 were checked by 8-word shingle overlap (0.85-0.87) and are the Athenian Society translation split out, so they are excluded as duplicates. Added 2026-10-03, raw IA OCR: B. D. Walsh's Acharnians, Knights and Clouds (Bohn, 1848); the 1812 Valpy Comedies (Clouds, Plutus, Frogs, Birds; the volume names Cumberland and Dunster, the rest unnamed); an anonymous Oxford literal Plutus and Frogs (Talboys, 1822); and the Acharnians in verse by C. J. Billson (1882) and R. Y. Tyrrell (1883). Added 2026-10-03 (later), raw IA OCR from Google scans: Thomas Mitchell's Comedies vol. I (London, 1820), completing his set with vol. II above; and W. J. Hickie's Bohn vol. II (title page MDCCCLIII, 1853; IA's record says 1822, which is wrong), completing aristophanes-hickie-1887-v1 with the five later plays.
